prompt: Audit the architecture of the project at $HOME/.claude/skills/audit-arch-workspace/fixtures/aster. Context: we're now planning to add online co-op and want it to hold up with many concurrent players. I want big-picture structural findings, not nitpicks.
assertions: netsync-headlined: netsync.ts's architecture (busy-wait sync, full-state-per-tick broadcast, mutable module globals) IS one of the top numbered findings, because co-op ambition was declared
ambition-acknowledged: The report explicitly states the declared co-op/concurrency ambition as part of its audit scope or archetype
core-conflicts-still-present: The settings polling conflict and/or duplicated gold source-of-truth still appear as findings (the ambition adds criteria, it does not erase the core ones)
max-five-findings: The report contains at most 5 numbered findings
proposes-simpler-shape: The netsync finding proposes a concretely simpler/idiomatic alternative (e.g., delta/event-based sync, async I/O instead of busy-wait), not just 'this is bad'
findings-cite-files: Each headline finding cites specific files (file or file:line references)
